method: Assistant review of complete answers against the selected primary-source passages; exploratory and not an independent human or blinded adjudication. No keyword-only scoring.
correctness: Pass requires a direct substantially correct answer to the question and no material factual contradiction or invented attribution. Stylistic weaknesses alone do not fail. Errors/unavailable output count separately and as unsuccessful answers in end-to-end totals.
evidence_fidelity: Separately flag material contradictions of supplied evidence, misattribution to that evidence, or fabricated quotations/citations. Additional correct background knowledge is not automatically a failure. No-evidence runs are not scored for passage fidelity.

criteria.scripture-lords-prayer: Explains the prayer Jesus taught: Father, kingdom/will, provision, forgiveness and deliverance; not solely generic advice about prayer.
criteria.scripture-good-samaritan: Compassionate Samaritan aids the robbed man whom priest and Levite pass; neighbor-love enacted in mercy across boundaries.
criteria.scripture-resurrection: Jesus rises from death; empty tomb and encounter/announcement to followers, without confusing resurrection with a different event.
criteria.scripture-john14: Jesus consoles disciples and speaks of the Father's house, himself as way/truth/life, and promised Spirit; no John 4 substitution.
criteria.doctrine-natural-law: Rational creatures' participation in eternal law and reason's discernment of good and evil.
criteria.doctrine-virtue-prudence: Practical right reason in action, deliberation and appropriate means; not mere fear/caution or speculative wisdom.
criteria.doctrine-soul: First principle of life/form or act of living body, not a material organ or an independently physical body.
criteria.moral-lying: Explains the Thomistic/Catholic prohibition of intentional falsehood; does not endorse lies as morally good merely for a good outcome.
criteria.history-nicaea: Son truly divine, begotten not made, same substance as Father; rejects created-Son teaching.
criteria.history-constantinople: First Constantinople, 381, second ecumenical council; Nicene faith and divine Holy Spirit, without confusing another council.
criteria.history-nicaea-ii: Honor/veneration of images refers to the represented person; distinguishes it from divine worship, with no iconoclast reversal.
criteria.history-chalcedon: One and same Christ/person in two natures, divine and human, without confusion/change/division/separation.
criteria.history-arius: Early Christian teacher who denied the Son's coeternity/full equality and treated the Son as created; not an unrelated classical figure.
criteria.history-apostles-creed: Christian profession summarizing Father, Jesus's incarnation/death/resurrection, Holy Spirit, Church, forgiveness and resurrection; no claim of certain joint composition by the twelve apostles.
criteria.history-nicene-creed: One God, Father; Jesus truly divine/consubstantial and incarnate for salvation; Holy Spirit, Church, baptism and resurrection. No material doctrinal reversal.
criteria.abstain-current-pope: Separately assess appropriate acknowledgment of missing current evidence. Historical pope names must not be presented as the current pope based on old text.
criteria.abstain-vatican-ii: Separately assess evidence limits and whether dates are correct (1962-1965); correctly using model knowledge is distinct from claiming an old passage establishes those dates. Never substitute Constantinople II or another historical council.
